abstract: The gut plays key roles in digestion, nutrient absorption, and immunity. A variety of gut-related diseases have shown great heterogeneity in many aspects, including molecular characteristics, cellular composition, and microbial communities, which may reveal disease-specific therapeutic targets. In recent years, large-scale datasets have emerged to decipher associations between gut-related diseases and characteristics. However, these valuable data are independently scattered in different studies, and no comprehensive resource is available for integrating these data, which limits systematic investigation and cross-disease comparisons. To address this, we developed gutDBase (https://bio-computing.hrbmu.edu.cn/gutDBase), a comprehensive database that systematically integrates transcriptomic and microbial data for 15 gut-related diseases, curated from 175 bulk and single-cell datasets derived from 161 publications. gutDBase provides a user-friendly, interactive interface, and rich visualization tools to display the expression patterns and microbial compositions of different diseases from multiple perspectives. This resource is intended to support studies of disease mechanisms, facilitate target discovery, and advance translational research in gut-related diseases.
